title: Inferring Microphysical Process Rates from in Situ Observations Using Physics-Informed Machine Learning (Invited Presentation)
testbed_rationale: Conference abstract without specific dataset identifiers, URLs, or access details.
pain_points: In situ atmospheric measurements from aircraft and ground-based instruments typically provide only static snapshots of cloud particle size distributions or ice crystal morphology at single points in space and time, making it challenging to infer dynamical microphysical process rates.
Traditional inverse modeling methods struggle to reconstruct microphysical tendencies such as collision-coalescence and depositional ice growth.
